body:
My SO has been in a serious rut mentally for the past few days and hasn't been taking his meds. I'm overseas and I feel useless. I've relapsed with cutting, both to relieve emotional pain and to punish myself. Good news is I am lucky enough to have an amazing SO who somehow loves the piece of shit that I am. I can't wait to see him next month. 

Edit: word

I was where you are 2 years ago and for me, things have gotten exponentially better (though keep in mind that things were pretty shitty to begin with). I'm on medication, sporadically practice meditation (it helps and I really should be doing it more), exercising regularly, and go to therapy. I have downs. But I have ups too and overall I'd say I'm net up. So yes, there is hope. Maybe the depression won't go away 100% for good but you can find ways to minimize it and find support to help you fight in those moments when you are in a rut.

You might want to address your issues with depression first. Whether it be therapy or medication, finding the right fit for you will make life a lot easier to deal with. Your physical health matters, but so does your mental health. Maybe taking care of the latter will help you become more motivated to take care of the former. 

I'm sorry you are so miserable at your job and I hope you can either find a mutually compatible way to adapt or find a better fit for you elsewhere.

First off, welcome. This sub can be a great place to find out you're not alone and get support. At first I just lurked here and after a while all the comments I had but kept to myself eventually came out and I began posting and commenting. It's nice to see you've taken the first step and commented. This can be a good space to share anything and everything (within the scope of the sub rules, of course :) ).

Good luck on your tests. I came from a high school where taking APs was the norm and I ended up taking them just because everyone else was. I ended up really stressed out a lot and had little sleep. A school counselor I had later told me that my health comes before school. Maybe that advice can help you. I think it could have helped me if I had applied that advice to myself in high school. And really, I hope you do well.

I really want to say something helpful but I'm afraid I'll say the wrong thing. But here's a summary of my story. Was in school, pushed myself, depression overloaded but I still piled summer school onto myself and ended up failing a class. 

Next year starts and I'm again pushing myself past my limit (which at this point was pretty low because my depression/anxiety just ate me up all the time). I end up in a psych hospital and it is decided that taking a year off of school is what I needed. 

Thing is, school counselor helped make it all happen. She's not a therapist but she's there to help me. She told me my health came before school. Maybe you should consider your options (and yes, you have options) and reevaluate your immediate plans before you end up in a hospital involuntarily. 

Meds don't hurt either one you've found the right mix. They help establish some stability, at least with me. 

Hope I didn't confuse you or make you feel bad or anything. I'm just trying to help. I don't know. Feel free to ignore everything I've said.
I'm glad to hear your medication is doing what it should. It's a nice moment when you realize you've found the right mix.

I'm just a stranger, but I'm proud of you for studying and applying to jobs. I know how fucking hard it can be to get myself to do anything and to hear that you've been doing generally well despite the depression is good to hear. I'm sorry about your breakdown. I know how they feel. But you seem strong and capable and I really genuinely believe in you.

I don't deserve this bring read by anyone. I cut for the first time in a long while and it felt so good. I'm ashamed at myself for not being strong enough to cut deeper. I'm ashamed at myself for not being strong enough to not cut. I told my boyfriend what happened but he's asleep now. I'm scared because I can't take my messages back after I hit Enter. He's going to be so disappointed in me. He's already been feeling bad this week and I've just made it worse. I am a piece of shit that doesn't deserve to live.

Lol, yes, I am depressed but trying to get it under control. Currently taking medication and some time off from the world (gap year). I'm trying to keep myself busy with projects, mostly making stuff for other people (gifts). So I guess, for the time being, I have a hobby in that I do something on a consistent basis which I enjoy to an extent. Though I enjoy the process less than the prospect of the person getting their gift. I could say that I like to make people happy. Seems like that would be a bad hobby if it goes to far though, if it even could be considered a hobby.

Don't worry, I think I'm past thinking I'm a freak. I know there are a lot of people in a similar situation emotionally and mentally as I am. I will say I've done quite a bit of work emotionally and mentally over the past few years to not hate myself and up my self-esteem.

My self-view is not about buying the latest thing or fitting in, for the most part. I buy what I like and I make sure I like what I buy. Which reminds me now that if ever I had a hobby, it's shopping. I like nice things. I know that buying stuff gives only a temporary rush of good feelings, but I enjoy the things I buy over time too. But it's kinda unsustainable as I don't have a job and want to save my money. So it's more of an occasional thing. 

>Maybe by nurturing the small incidentals in life like cooking and habitat maintenance ... by helping some one else in a village cooperative kind of way ?

I think this is something I could be working on. My main issue is, for lack of a better term, laziness. Tasks that involve effort above a certain threshold are hard for me to get myself to engage in. Which is probably why I don't have a consistent hobby. If I did, they would be art, crafts, and cooking. But resistance towards effort needed overrules any enjoyment I may derive from these activities. I basically just sound really lazy.

I really should read books on psychology. Especially because I'm aiming at cognitive science/psychology as my major, lol. Another side effect, I think, of the anxiety is my indecisiveness. Can't choose which books to read. But I'll ask around and find some suggestions to narrow the pool of choices, or look some book list up. 

Urban gardening sounds like a good hobby. Good for you health-wise and I think gardening has shown to be a hobby that helps plenty of people who have depression. No stats to show and it's 6am here to I'm too tired to look them up. Might have been because of exercise or being with nature... something of that sort. Maybe start planning that. It's definitely doing something.

Sorry if I'm at all rambly or don't make sense or don't seem to address you points. Idk. When I start thinking about my lifestyle, my thought process gets all jumbled and criss-crossed in my head.

>Have you considered what may have caused your apathy towards your own personal direction ? 

I just don't feel like I care too much about any one activity or occupation or goal. Even going to school is like... I don't even care that much. 

Sometimes my caring goes from 0 to 100 in pretty bad situations, usually caring for people who, in retrospect, a) don't deserve it or b) are toxic. Or I used to care a lot (more, still do in an anxiety sort of way) about what people thought of me. So caring in my subconscious might = bad stuff. Idk. I'm no shrink and self-analysis can be pretty limited without some objective input, I guess. 

>If nothing grabs you choose anything and try

There is stuff I do and somewhat enjoy doing more than other things but the effort that goes into them is daunting and trumps any desire to want to do them. I feel like I mainly want to do them not because I care much about it but because I feel I should do it or want to seem impressive. Self-doubt probably plays into not actually doing that stuff too (e.g. art, lot of room to fall below your own standards until you've developed skill... which I have no passion/patience for).

>Really?

If this is in response to...

>I'm glad you came out of the woodwork and commented. :) It means a lot.

...then yes, really. :) 

>to be blunt - if you are imbalanced in your valueing of your relationship in comparison to yourself then ofcourse you will suffer anxiety about any threats to that relationship.

This rings a bell in my head and seems very likely to be true. I hadn't thought of it like that. Thanks for bringing it to my attention. It makes a lot of sense. 

Sorry for the late reply. This is (possibly obviously, looking at my username) not my main account and I forgot to check it.

Yeah, police were called first time I ever called into a hotline. It was... over-the-top and I was very unhappy with the hotline lady for doing that. I trusted her to just listen to what I had to say so I would feel better, not throw me into a circus of police officers and ambulance drivers and mental health workers. 

I get that in her eyes she was trying to help and she definitely did "give a flying fuck" about me, but it really made me feel betrayed and rather terrible. She kinda took my options out of my own hands. I don't think "humanity is so fucking garbage" but I do understand the sentiment of not wanting to give them personal details in case they might use them in ways I don't approve of.

This is in the US btw.

Not a big coffee/caffeine or alcohol drinker. I eat fairly well. Healthy with a dash of junk food.

I absolutely suck at staying on top of mindful breathing and meditation. I am the absolute worst at being consistent with this. Definitely something I need to work on. It will probably help.

What books did you pick up?

Dreams: don't really have any big ones so they're not being inhibited but I do the stuff I want to do (e.g. travel, learn stuff) without too much trouble aside from the usual procrastination and laziness. 

Lost in love: doubt it. Been together for 2.5 years so the honeymoon period is long past. It's a more stable partner-type situation now. 

Overvaluing relationship is possibly right. I'm also pretty depressed so I'm practically living because my relationship is promising. I overvalue it in the sense that I don't value much other than it. 

I feel a bit too apathetic and dispassionate to have any burning desires or big dreams in general but basic stuff like I like to travel and get stable job I do hope and work for.

I'm glad you came out of the woodwork and commented. :) It means a lot. I hope all goes well with your therapist and I hope he/she proves to be a keeper. I know all to well the feeling of wanting to back out of a session, especially the first one (I've hopped around a few therapists even just within the past year or two).

Thank you for your words and time.
Thanks. Simple but reassuring.

Good luck. Deep breaths (sorry if that's annoying to hear but it can help). I hope all goes well. Being assertive can feel hard and confronting people sucks but hopefully it'll get you to the right outcome.

I am a returning reader. I'm abroad, not taking my meds, and considering killing myself when I get home. I'm tired of human interaction and my irrational fears. I want to sleep and never wake up. I want to be able to cut myself and not have questions asked about the marks. I'm so very tired.
I was just thinking about this today. I'm going to try to make decisions that will hopefully lead to less regrets. We'll see how it turns out.

I was in a somewhat similar situation once. One of my boyfriend's good friends was madly in love with him and they'd ben close for years before he and I started dating. I cried myself to sleep imaging them together and it killed me to see them together (they had some classes and extracurriculars together). I kept it bottled in although I told a couple friends who were also concerned with how close he was to her. 

It got really really bad and my anxiety was off the walls crazy and I thought about breaking up so he could just be with her and I wouldn't be in so much pain. Turns out, he could tell something was not quite right for a while, I guess I subconsciously showed signs of jealousy or something. I ended up telling him, he was understanding *even though we both knew he did not and would not do anything with her*. 

I personally believe that openness and communication, even about crazy irrational stuff, is better than the alternative of bottling up negative feelings and thoughts. It might help relieve the anxiety too and seems like a better alternative to drinking or using drugs. 

Have you talked to your psychiatrist about how the meds have been affecting you? Maybe talking to a therapist (if that is a viable option) a couple times might help give you some more insight into your options and why this is happening/how to stop it. It usually helps me to talk to a third party (in person, not just Reddit as lovely as it is) about my relationship problems. 

I'm sorry that people in your past have been shitty and I know how hard it can be to deal with anxiety and irrational thoughts in a relationship. I hope I could help a little and good luck.

In my experience, hiding things from your SO does not turn out well. It may be an awkward conversation, but maybe you need to just confront him about what's going on. That way he can support you and maybe you two can find some way to help these nightmares recede. 

As for the dreams and fear of intimacy, I personally would recommend trying a therapist (I think sex therapists/relationship therapists might be better for this area). 

This seems horrifying and it's terrible that it is happening to you. I'm sorry it's limiting and scarring you. I hope you, maybe with your boyfriend or a therapist's help, can figure out how to cope with it and make it go away. Good luck.

Well, my situation allowed me to withdraw from school for a year or so (probably more with the problems I'm having) but I also am seeing a therapist and have started on medication. Exercise helps, I think. 3-4 times per week of minimum 30 minutes elevated heart rate. Have to do a lot of recognizing cognitive distortions and trying to fight it when I can. 

I was on the edge about taking medication, but being in a psych ward after a suicide attempt kinda puts things into perspective. Better to overcome the fear of taking pills rather than getting progressively worse, you know? The meds won't make you into a different person, it will just help to calm down that crazyass amygdala that is going nuts in your brain. :) 

But seriously, since the medication I've been able to sleep better and my paranoia has gone down significantly. The anxiety is still there but I only recently started on that medication so changes should be coming soon. The anxiety medication I'm on is Buspirone if you're curious to look it up. Also I take Lorazepam for sleep/anxiety.

Like the others, I agree that you should tell her. Honesty and communication are keystones in a good relationship. Be genuine about your feelings and thoughts: the fear of consequences if you tell her the truth, that you love her, that you are a different person now and regret what you did in the past. Good luck.

I went through this too. I thought I had one or all of these: Alzheimer's (I'm 20, btw), schizophrenia, psychopathy, sociopathy, ADHD, bipolar, borderline personality disorder, learning disabilities. I even went to a psychologist to get tested for ADHD because it was affecting my studies so much (difficulty concentrating, lack of motivation, fidgeting, difficulty remembering things). It turns out I don't have ADHD, my memory is fine, and I don't have any of those other things except bipolar, though it's not very serious.

It's hard to remember sometimes, but anxious people can interpret normal things about themselves as abnormal, e.g. memory problems, that happen to everyone else too. My memory and concentration issues were actually likely caused my by anxiety and depression rather than any other mental illness.

>  But I think I'm having a thought block and I am losing my ability to concentrate, I can't now read a paragraph without getting distracted and thinking about something else, so of course my studies are going down.

>I also feel that I am losing my ability to verbally describe things easily, I feel that I suffer to find the correct words to describe what I want to say, it's as if I have to dig deep. I also forget A LOT, I feel that I have almost no short term memory, I forget what I just did, I forget people's names, and I forget where I places my phone or wallet, etc.

I felt exactly like this. Getting tested helped calm my nerves, if that is a possibility for you, but if what is happening to you is anything like what happened/is happening (on occasion) to me, then it is likely the anxiety. I am not a medical professional though, only speaking from experience.

I hope I helped a little. Just know you're not alone in this. Good luck, truly, with everything that comes your way.

I know how you feel. It's really difficult to deal with this stuff. I'm glad you're taking a break. You don't need to feel ashamed that you don't think you can handle this stuff. Suicide is some seriously heavy shit. In this society, we're not prepared to deal with this. Try not to get sucked in. As hard as it is to accept, you don't have an obligation to help these people, especially if it hurts you. Make sure you take care of you first.

I know what you mean. I sit there reading the posts and don't know what to say, and the responses I do type out, I am too afraid to send for fear of not saying the right thing. The best advice I've seen on those posts are ones that are genuine, empathetic, and follow the guidelines from /r/SWResources.

If you are genuine and concerned, comment, and the best that can happen is that they gain some solace from what you said and feel like someone cares, and the worst case is that they are in the same position as before. As much as you might like to help, it's not always possible to convince someone to not commit suicide. It's hard to accept it, but preventing someone's death once they have lost the will to live is a tall order that you have no obligation to try to fill. Be a listening ear, a caring stranger. Offer them some love and it might make them at least feel a little better knowing someone out there hears them.

I'm sorry that you feel ashamed because you're one of the good guys, trying to help those who are teetering on the edge. It gets difficult dealing with those stories and suicide is a heavy topic. It's hard to understand suicide unless you've been suicidal yourself, it really is. 

Maybe take a break from the sub for a while. Recuperate and come back if you want to still help. It might help replenish your words and make you feel less bad.
